scenes.tts: These methane-making microbes look like typical bacteria. Why would a molecule place them on a different branch? Under the microscope, both are tiny cells without nuclei. Shape gives us evidence, but it may hide the ancestry we want to test.
scenes.caption: These methane-making microbes look like typical bacteria. Why would a molecule place them on a different branch? Under the microscope, both are tiny cells without nuclei. Shape gives us evidence, but it may hide the ancestry we want to test.
scenes.visual: COLOR MAP for both films: methane makers teal; typical Bacteria blue; Eukarya gold; evidence white. Fill the frame with one teal and one blue cartoon cell inside a moving microscope ring. Both cells slowly rotate. The ring stretches into an unresolved two-tip tree marked 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: These methane-making microbes look like typical bacteria. Why would a molecule place them on a different branch? Under the microscope, both are tiny cells without nuclei. Shape gives us evidence, but it may hide the ancestry we want to test.

scenes.visual: Keep the unresolved tree moving gently. Write the title 'The Molecule Behind the Tree' above it, then transform the title into a small label at the tree's base.

scenes.tts: To compare very different cells, scientists need the same kind of record from every sample. Every cell builds proteins on ribosomes. Ribosomal RNA forms much of each ribosome. Conserved parts let researchers line up distant samples, while differing parts provide evidence.
scenes.caption: To compare very different cells, scientists need the same kind of record from every sample. Every cell builds proteins on ribosomes. Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) forms much of each ribosome. Conserved parts let researchers line up distant samples, while differing parts provide evidence.
scenes.visual: The teal and blue cells slide apart. A gold nucleated cell joins them. Each opens a large labelled block 'ribosome', then the same white strip labelled 'ribosomal RNA'. Matching strip sections pulse together while a few sections change colour. No molecular structure.
scenes.narration: To compare very different cells, scientists need the same kind of record from every sample. Every cell builds proteins on ribosomes. Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) forms much of each ribosome. Conserved parts let researchers line up distant samples, while differing parts provide evidence.

scenes.tts: Woese and Fox compared catalogues of short ribosomal RNA pieces. Picture each catalogue as a row of labelled tiles, not a complete molecule. Matching tiles pull the rows together. Fewer matches leave the rows farther apart. The pattern across pairs tests the tree.
scenes.caption: Woese and Fox compared catalogues of short ribosomal RNA pieces. Picture each catalogue as a row of labelled tiles, not a complete molecule. Matching tiles pull the rows together. Fewer matches leave the rows farther apart. The pattern across pairs tests the tree.
scenes.visual: Transform each white strip into six large labelled tiles. Teal-to-teal tiles gain many bright links and move closer. Teal-to-blue tiles gain few links and drift apart. Keep the unresolved tree visible at right with its branch joint wobbling. Mark the tile model 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Woese and Fox compared catalogues of short ribosomal RNA pieces. Picture each catalogue as a row of labelled tiles, not a complete molecule. Matching tiles pull the rows together. Fewer matches leave the rows farther apart. The pattern across pairs tests the tree.

scenes.tts: Here are hidden pairs. A pair shares many ribosomal RNA pieces, while another shares few. Which pair should sit closer on a tree of ancestry? Hold your answer before the labels appear.
scenes.caption: Here are hidden pairs. A pair shares many ribosomal RNA pieces, while another shares few. Which pair should sit closer on a tree of ancestry? Hold your answer before the labels appear.
scenes.visual: Two large anonymous tile pairs replace the labelled rows. The left pair has many white links; the right has few. A question mark travels between each pair and two empty branch positions. Keep all tiles slowly drifting.
scenes.narration: Here are hidden pairs. A pair shares many ribosomal RNA pieces, while another shares few. Which pair should sit closer on a tree of ancestry? Hold your answer before the labels appear.

scenes.visual: Hold the predict question. Let the many-match pair breathe closer and the few-match pair breathe apart without revealing labels. A thin progress arc sweeps once around the question mark.

scenes.tts: The pair with many shared pieces belongs closer, if the rest of the evidence agrees. The methane makers matched each other far better than they matched typical bacteria. Typical bacteria also matched each other better than they matched methane makers. That repeated pattern challenged a combined prokaryote group.
scenes.caption: The pair with many shared pieces belongs closer, if the rest of the evidence agrees. The methane makers matched each other far better than they matched typical bacteria. Typical bacteria also matched each other better than they matched methane makers. That repeated pattern challenged a combined prokaryote group.
scenes.visual: Reveal teal labels on the many-match pair and blue labels on a pair with a moderate number of links: fewer than the teal pair, more than the teal-blue pair. Show a teal-blue pair with few links. Each pair pulls on the matching tree tips. The old combined branch bends but does not snap until all three patterns are visible.

scenes.tts: A classification is a testable map of relationships. A branch claims that its members share a more recent common ancestor. When several comparisons challenge that claim, scientists redraw only the supported part. The organisms themselves remain unchanged.
scenes.caption: A classification is a testable map of relationships. A branch claims that its members share a more recent common ancestor. When several comparisons challenge that claim, scientists redraw only the supported part. The organisms themselves remain unchanged.
scenes.visual: Turn the tree into a flexible map with hinged branch joints. A white 'ancestry claim' tag attaches to one joint. Three evidence links pull that joint into a new position while every teal and blue microbe icon keeps its shape.
scenes.narration: A classification is a testable map of relationships. A branch claims that its members share a more recent common ancestor. When several comparisons challenge that claim, scientists redraw only the supported part. The organisms themselves remain unchanged.

scenes.tts: The researchers interpreted this pattern as three major lines of descent. Later, the rank called domain named Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya. The methane makers joined Archaea. Their cells did not change. The evidence changed the best-supported tree.
scenes.caption: The researchers interpreted this pattern as three major lines of descent. Later, the rank called domain named Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya. The methane makers joined Archaea. Their cells did not change. The evidence changed the best-supported tree.
scenes.visual: The branch joint settles into three wide branches. Blue Bacteria, teal Archaea and gold Eukarya labels grow from their matching tips. Keep the original microbes unchanged as their labels move. The dates '1977' and '1990' appear silently below the two revisions, then fade.
scenes.narration: The researchers interpreted this pattern as three major lines of descent. Later, the rank called domain named Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya. The methane makers joined Archaea. Their cells did not change. The evidence changed the best-supported tree.

scenes.tts: Molecular evidence does not automatically outrank every other clue. It adds a comparison that can expose misleading similarities in shape. Strong classifications weigh several markers and kinds of evidence. Agreement strengthens a branch. Conflict shows where to test next.
scenes.caption: Molecular evidence does not automatically outrank every other clue. It adds a comparison that can expose misleading similarities in shape. Strong classifications weigh several markers and kinds of evidence. Agreement strengthens a branch. Conflict shows where to test next.
scenes.visual: Around the carried tree, balance large evidence cards labelled 'structure', 'development', 'RNA' and 'DNA'. Cards that agree stack beside one joint. A conflicting card turns into a question mark that moves toward a different branch joint.
scenes.narration: Molecular evidence does not automatically outrank every other clue. It adds a comparison that can expose misleading similarities in shape. Strong classifications weigh several markers and kinds of evidence. Agreement strengthens a branch. Conflict shows where to test next.

scenes.tts: The overlap scores are not percentages of DNA. They do not tell when branches split. They summarize shared pieces in these ribosomal RNA catalogues. A tree remains a claim tested against more organisms, other genes, membranes and any evidence that can challenge it.
scenes.caption: The overlap scores are not percentages of DNA. They do not tell when branches split. They summarize shared pieces in these ribosomal RNA catalogues. A tree remains a claim tested against more organisms, other genes, membranes and any evidence that can challenge it.
scenes.visual: Keep the three-colour tree centered. A percent sign and clock approach, then slide aside without red rejection marks. Evidence cards labelled 'more organisms', 'other genes' and 'membranes' orbit the branch joints. Mark the tree 'best-supported model'.
scenes.narration: The overlap scores are not percentages of DNA. They do not tell when branches split. They summarize shared pieces in these ribosomal RNA catalogues. A tree remains a claim tested against more organisms, other genes, membranes and any evidence that can challenge it.

scenes.tts: That is why changing a group after careful testing can be good science. Classification is a model of ancestry, not a permanent filing cabinet. When stronger evidence changes the picture, scientists revise the model while keeping its limits visible.
scenes.caption: That is why changing a group after careful testing can be good science. Classification is a model of ancestry, not a permanent filing cabinet. When stronger evidence changes the picture, scientists revise the model while keeping its limits visible.
scenes.visual: The tree folds briefly into a filing cabinet, then unfolds back into the living three-colour tree. New white evidence brightens one branch joint. A small 'limits' tag stays beside the base as the camera moves closer.
scenes.narration: That is why changing a group after careful testing can be good science. Classification is a model of ancestry, not a permanent filing cabinet. When stronger evidence changes the picture, scientists revise the model while keeping its limits visible.

scenes.visual: Show one centered line only: 'Classification changes when new evidence changes the best-supported picture of ancestry.' Keep the teal, blue and gold branches moving faintly behind it.
